items.stem: Classify each entity as People, Org structure, or Access: (1) Staff, (2) Wards, (3) Standalone Groups. Which mapping is correct?

options.text: Staff = People, Wards = Org structure, Standalone Groups = Access
Staff = Access, Wards = People, Standalone Groups = Org structure
Staff = Org structure, Wards = Access, Standalone Groups = People
All three are Access entities

items.explanation: Staff are people; Wards are an org/geographic structure; Standalone Groups are an access (membership) construct.

misconceptions.b: Staff are people, not an access role; Wards are geographic structure, not people.
misconceptions.c: Staff aren't org structure; Wards aren't access.
misconceptions.d: Only Standalone Groups is an access entity here.

items.stem: What are the three Data-Owner security-group families in SDM?

options.text: Department, School, and Functional-Site Data Owners
Admin, Editor, and Viewer
Staff, Vendor, and Trustee
Read, Write, and Delete

items.explanation: SDM has Department, School, and Functional-Site Data Owners — AAD-backed groups granting editing rights over their area.

misconceptions.b: Those are generic role names, not SDM's data-owner families.
misconceptions.c: Those are other entities, not the data-owner families.
misconceptions.d: Those are permission verbs, not the data-owner groups.

items.stem: How does a Standalone Group differ from a Data Owner group?

options.text: A Standalone Group is a hand-maintained membership list that doesn't sync from upstream; a Data Owner group is an AAD-backed role granting rights
They are the same thing with different names
A Standalone Group grants admin rights; a Data Owner group is just a list
Standalone Groups exist only in PowerSchool

items.explanation: Standalone Groups are static lists maintained directly in SDM (simple or composite); Data Owners are AAD-group-backed roles that grant editing rights.

misconceptions.b: They're distinct: one is a hand-maintained list, the other a group-backed role.
misconceptions.c: It's the reverse — Data Owners grant rights; Standalone Groups are membership lists.
misconceptions.d: Standalone Groups are managed in SDM and written to DDH.

items.stem: When a user edits an entity in SDM, what records who made the change?

options.text: The CreatedBy / UpdatedBy audit fields (with an AuditLog), written to DDH
Nothing — SDM doesn't track who changed data
A comment the user types each time
The browser's history

items.explanation: Domain entities carry CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit fields and an AuditLog in DDH, so every change records who made it.

misconceptions.c: Audit is automatic on the entity, not a manual comment.
misconceptions.d: Audit lives in DDH, not the browser.

items.stem: A colleague reports: "The School Data Owner for School 001 is wrong, and a standalone group's membership is also off." Using SDM's entity map, where do these two issues live, and what do they have in common?
rubric: Places both under the Access bucket: School Data Owner is one of the three Data-Owner families; the standalone group is a Standalone Group membership list
Notes they are different mechanisms (group-backed role vs. hand-maintained list)
Notes the edits are made in SDM and written to DDH with audit
items.sampleAnswer: Both are access concerns. The School Data Owner is one of SDM's three Data-Owner families (an AAD-backed role), while the standalone group's membership is a hand-maintained Standalone Group list — different mechanisms, but both about who can do what. You'd correct each in its SDM area, and the edits write to DDH with CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit.

items.stem: Beyond being static membership lists, what are Standalone Groups also used for in SDM?

options.text: Role-based access — the Help Desk grants temporary access via Entra (AAD) group memberships through the Standalone Group menu
Storing each user's password
Running the nightly sync jobs
Defining school attendance areas

items.explanation: Role-based access was lifted into SDM from the old config JSON; Standalone Groups are how the Help Desk grants temporary access via Entra group memberships.

misconceptions.b: SDM stores no credentials; access is via Entra group membership, not passwords.
misconceptions.c: The Sync-* fleet runs the syncs, not Standalone Groups.
misconceptions.d: Attendance areas belong to Schools, not Standalone Groups.
